quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: If the throttle is stuck, what should you do?

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Do not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, try twisting it back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, turn off the engine using the cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, which part of the lane should you ride in?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
Either the left or right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing parked cars. This keeps you away from opening car doors, people stepping out between cars, and cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding during the day?

options.text: Do not use either your low beam or high beam headlight.

questions.explanation: Use your high beam headlight during the day for the best visibility.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting the animal.
Switch lanes as quickly as possible.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane when an animal enters it. Swerving into another lane can cause you to crash into another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is less dangerous than hitting another car.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which of these does NOT need to be adjusted?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle will sit lower with a passenger. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. The brake light position does not need to be adjusted.

questions.question: What will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down and use both brakes. Avoid sudden moves and do not ride in the center of the lane. Follow the tire tracks left by cars. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: In hot weather, should you wear a riding jacket?

options.text: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
No, it can cause heat-related problems.
Only if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it helps protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Always wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They provide safety benefits and help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down suddenly if a vehicle is following you too closely. This warns the driver behind you that you are stopping.

questions.question: What type of sign is rectangular?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that inform drivers of road rules, like speed limits, are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When do most motorcycle crashes happen?

options.text: After riding for a long time.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on short trips of less than five miles at speeds slower than 30 miles per hour.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help prevent fatigue on a long ride?

options.text: Limit how far you ride in one day.

questions.explanation: To prevent fatigue while riding, dress to stay warm and protect yourself from wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take a break at least every two hours. Do not take artificial stimulants. You may experience extreme fatigue when they wear off.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while turning a curve?

options.text: It works the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip on the road as you lean.
You may have less grip on the road as you lean.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip on the road as you lean.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. Your tires use some grip to make the turn while leaning. This means less grip is available for stopping.

questions.question: What does a linked braking system do?

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either brake is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter so the brake applies when you downshift.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes work when either brake is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either the front or rear brake lever, both brakes get braking pressure. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: When someone is following you too closely.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your turn signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When someone is following you too closely.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down if someone is following you too closely. The other driver may not notice an upcoming hazard that is causing you to slow. Also flash your brake light when you are about to slow down in an unexpected place.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before you hit it.
Slow down before you hit it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you hit it.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle in the road, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel just before you hit it.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks that run parallel to the road, you should:

options.text: Cross at a 45-degree angle or steeper.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at a 45-degree angle or steeper.
questions.explanation: To safely cross railroad tracks, trolley tracks, or road seams that run parallel to your lane, move to a position where you can cross them at least at a 45-degree angle. Make a quick, sharp turn. If you try to cross slowly, the tracks or seam can catch your tire and throw you off balance.

questions.question: In normal conditions, what following distance should you keep behind the vehicle ahead?
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane provides three paths of travel for a motorcyclist: the left side, the center, and the right side of the lane.

questions.question: Why should you not change gears on railroad tracks?

options.text: Other drivers may not expect you to shift gears.
The uneven surface may make shifting difficult.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. There is a risk that your motorcycle may stall while you are on the tracks.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, which headlight setting should you use?

options.text: Switch between low and high beam.

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight when riding in rain, snow, or fog. A high beam reflects off these conditions and makes it harder to see.

questions.question: When making a normal stop, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Switch between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing down or stopping, including for normal stops.

questions.question: If you need to brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both actions at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Perform braking and swerving one after the other, not at the same time. You can brake then swerve, or swerve then brake.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids when you are braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and let the vehicle coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately and then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Apply the rear brake firmly while slowly increasing the front brake pressure.

questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.
